title: partial-capacity-communications-and-differentiation-notes
summary: Working brief for standardized customer-facing communications and internal scripts when Redwood experiences partial capacity constraints, region-specific throttling, or degraded feature sets. Focused on preserving trust through transparent, actionable messaging and on highlighting product-level differentiation vs. competitors who default to blanket downtimes or opaque throttles.
objectives: Create short, reusable scripts for phone/email/chat for three audience tiers: developers (self-serve), platform/infra teams, and executive sponsors.
Map technical fallback options to plain-language customer impact statements so SAs can quickly set expectations.
Capture competitive gaps that translate into talking points (e.g., competitor X has single-region fallbacks; Redwood supports cross-region transparent failover with pinned model behavior).
Identify required collateral (status page copy, email templates, KB updates, canned Slack responses) and owners.
key_messages: We design for continuity: when capacity is reduced we route intelligently by region, model variant, and cost tier to keep critical operations available.
Transparent fallback: customers see which model/region is serving their request and what quality tradeoffs (latency, response length) to expect.
Predictable degradations: we prefer controlled, documented tradeoffs (quantized model fallback, reduced max tokens) over opaque throttles.
Safety nets: automatic canaries and rollbacks reduce blast-radius; our Console shows token-level cost and latency during incidents so teams can triage quickly.
incident_scenarios: Scenario A — Regional GPU exhaustion: sudden spike in eu-west causing queued requests. Observable impact: higher p95 latency, some 503s on non-critical routes. Response: route new requests to eu-central fallback pool + smaller-quant model variant for non-realtime flows.

Scenario B — Model-serving regression after deploy: degraded quality on a subset of prompts. Observable impact: increased error-rate in evals, customer QA flags. Response: automatic rollback to prior model version + canned customer communication offering mitigation steps and optional private rollout.

Scenario C — Control plane outage for select customers (Private): inability to create new keys or change rollouts. Observable impact: no inference disruption for running workers but reduced management ability. Response: clearly communicate scope, provide timeline, and offer manual ops assistance.
fallback_options_table:
Option | Impact on customer | When to use | Owner
--- | --- | --- | ---
Model-variant degrade (quantized/smaller) | Slightly lower fidelity, lower cost & latency | High queueing or GPU shortage for non-critical gen | Serving-runtime ops
Regional reroute | Potential increase in network latency, identical model version if available | Partial region outage or capacity pressure | Smart-routing team
Reduced max_tokens / streaming chunking | Shorter outputs or more incremental streaming | When tail-latency spikes and token costs matter | Platform engineering
Graceful 429 with retry-hint | Short interruption with explicit retry guidance | Burst limits hit for tenant | Rate-limiting infra
Read-only control plane + manual support | No change to running inference; admin actions delayed | Control plane incident affecting Private customers | Customer success + SRE
customer_scripts: Developer (chat): "We hit short capacity constraints in your region. To keep your app responsive we’re routing some requests to a nearby region and using a slightly smaller model for non-critical traffic — you may notice shorter replies for a brief window. We’ll notify you when full capacity is restored; if you want persistent regional isolation, we can sketch Dedicated options."

Platform lead (email): "Hi — quick update on yesterday’s elevated P95s: we automatically rerouted non-critical inference to a nearby region and engaged the quantized fallback. This kept latency under your SLA for core routes. Attached are the console links showing per-route token breakdown and suggested config changes to avoid recurrence. Shall we schedule a 30-minute runbook review?"

Executive sponsor (phone): "We had targeted degradation to protect uptime for critical workflows. We prioritized your high-throughput routes and enabled automatic fallbacks; the tradeoff was slight reduction in output length for background jobs. We’ll follow up with a short post-incident note and an offer for a Dedicated capacity assessment."
support_playbook_notes: Always surface one concrete action customers can take (temporarily reduce batch size, pin to a lower-latency model, enable caching) — this reduces perceived helplessness.
If the incident affects only non-prod routes, state that explicitly and provide guidance for toggling routing rules in the Console.
Don’t use absolutes: prefer 'we're routing' over 'we have failed over' when behavior is partial — maintains trust without overpromising.
competitive_gaps: Competitor A: single-region failover — leads to larger blast radius for region outages. Talk track: Redwood supports multi-region routing with per-tenant policies and visible fallback reasons.
Competitor B: opaque throttles — customers often don't know why prompts are failing. Talk track: Redwood exposes fallbacks in Console + logs so teams can make config changes proactively.

Open-source runtimes: good performance but heavy ops burden for customers. Talk track: Redwood offers same-grade runtime optimizations with managed observability and optional Dedicated/private deployment.
recommended_assets: Short status-page templates for partial degradations (multi-region routing, model-variant fallback). Owner: comms.
One-pager: 'How Redwood degrades safely' — visual flowchart for SAs. Owner: GTM enablement.
Console quick-links: prefilled filter to show 'fallback' traces during incidents. Owner: product console team.
Email templates: dev, platform, exec variants + post-incident summary. Owner: customer success.

- Quick win: add canned Slack responses for #support-escalations for common fallback cases.
- Pricing convo: be ready to propose Dedicated or Reserved pools when customers demand no cross-region routing.
- Follow-ups: sync with infra team (INC-2024-09-12 notes) and product (PRD: fallback-policy-ux).
